T0612.title: Adversarial Patch
T0612.definition: A physical adversarial example crafted by an attacker, printed and placed on an object or in a scene, that makes a robot's visual perception misidentify objects, grab wrong items, or avoid wrong targets.
T0612.description: Adversarial patches are the main vehicle of physical-world adversarial attacks, needing to overcome lighting, viewpoint, and distance variation to remain effective after physical-world printing. VLA-targeted patch attacks hijack text-visual attention (Patch Attention Dominance) or disrupt visual-text latent-alignment, persistently disturbing robot manipulation decisions in black-box, unknown-architecture, and sim-to-real transfer scenarios. UPA-RFAS (CVPR 2026) achieves single-patch black-box cross-model transfer, dropping task success by up to 100%. VLA-Attacker implements spatially-grounded untargeted/targeted attacks. Classic research like Evtimov's RP2 algorithm makes stop signs disappear with black-and-white stickers. Adversarial patches are the core attack vehicle of R0267 (physical-world prompt injection) and R0271 (VLA adversarial attack).
T0612.usageExample: An attacker placing an adversarial patch at a sorting-robot workstation may cause the robot to persistently grab wrong materials, causing a production incident.
